title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
author: Anthropic
takes: Context rot and an attention budget: more tokens, worse recall. Three tools for long work - compaction (risks losing what matters later), structured notes outside the window (NOTES.md), sub-agents that return 1-2 thousand token summaries; load knowledge just in time by reference.

title: Diátaxis: a systematic approach to technical documentation
author: Daniele Procida
takes: Four kinds by the reader's need - tutorial, how-to, reference, explanation - never mixed on one page. Reference is neutral and looked up: in a tad base, the tables; how-to is the named records and briefs; explanation is decisions, concepts and the occasional essay.

title: The /llms.txt file
author: Jeremy Howard
takes: One Markdown file at a fixed path: a title, a one-line summary, then sections of links with a note each, and an Optional section an agent may skip when short of context. A router, not the content.

title: AGENTS.md
author: agents.md
takes: A README for agents; the nearest AGENTS.md to the file being edited wins. The one file every agent already looks for - the place for a base's single entry.

title: Documenting Architecture Decisions
author: Michael Nygard
takes: One significant decision per record, numbered and never reused; a reversed decision is kept, marked superseded, pointing at what replaced it. docs' decisions table is this, with rejected beside it.

title: MADR: Markdown Architectural Decision Records 4.0
author: MADR project
takes: Adds considered options with pros and cons and a status that says superseded by which. What docs' decisions already keep as decision, why, rejected.

title: Data Package (Frictionless Data)
author: Frictionless Data
takes: datapackage.json at the top is the descriptor and index of the data's resources, each with a stable name and a schema. tables.toml follows its Table Schema; tad statements is the same kind of index for questions.

title: Docs as Code
author: Write the Docs
takes: Documentation in plain text, in git, reviewed and tested like code. What every tad base already is.

title: Evergreen notes
author: Andy Matuschak
takes: Atomic, concept-oriented, densely linked notes whose titles work like APIs; outline notes link many notes. One row is one such note; a checked link is the dense link; a query is the outline note.

title: Johnny.Decimal
author: Johnny Noble
takes: A fixed small index - no more than ten at each level - kept as a first-class record of every id. A base's entry should be that small.

title: The PARA Method
author: Tiago Forte
takes: Organise by actionability: projects, areas, resources, archives. In a base, what is actionable is read off status (open backlog), not filed by folder.

title: Help:Statements (Wikidata)
author: Wikidata
takes: Every statement is about an item, by its id, with references saying who says so. The missing piece in docs: records say which place they are of, but not checked which thing they are about.

title: Help:Infobox (Wikipedia)
author: Wikipedia
takes: A fixed-format summary of facts beside the prose that explains them; the facts must stand in the prose with citations too. Tables for facts, prose for reasons.

title: Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills
author: Zhang, Lazuka and Murag (Anthropic)
takes: Three levels: a name and one line always loaded, the body when relevant, linked files only when needed; scripts run without being read. The shape of a base's entry: AGENTS.md, tad statements, a query's rows, one row.

title: Manage Claude's memory (Claude Code)
author: Anthropic
takes: CLAUDE.md up the tree loads at start, nested ones when their subtree is touched; under 200 lines; imports organise but do not save context; procedures go into skills. CLAUDE.md is @AGENTS.md, one source.

title: PhotoCraft AGENTS.md
author: storytold
takes: Root AGENTS.md: who it is, then an Orientation table (Read / Why) of about 14 docs pages, the workspace map, golden rules, how to pick work, and where each thing is tracked and which pages are generated from which data. ArtCraft (storytold/artcraft) routes by nested AGENTS.md and .claude/rules instead.

title: Simplifying docs for AI with /llms.txt
author: Tiffany Chen (Mintlify)
takes: llms.txt as the slim index and llms-full.txt as the whole site in one file, both generated. For a base's published site, generated from the data - not the agent's entry.

title: text-as-data-template
author: creation-guidelines
takes: The commons' template for a knowledge base kept as data; last changed 2026-11-04 and still describing the vendored Python engine on a DuckDB schema (bin/adopt-engine.sh, .tad/), which every base left for tad on 2026-11-11.
